subject: GPU queueing spike and reserved throughput shortfall — CEO sync requested
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@parklinefin.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@parklinefin.com>
Date: Sun, 6 Sep 2026 21:03:00 -0700
Subject: Parkline production timeout wave — seeing 5xx + large p99 latency

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Quick note — over the last 70 minutes we've been seeing a sharp rise in user-facing timeouts for our document-processing flows. Error mix is ~60% 502/503 and persistent p99 token latency jumps from ~220ms -> ~2.1s. This is across our dedicated pool (reserved capacity), not the hosted path. Our telemetry shows queue depth growing and sustained requeueing, which is causing customer-facing timeouts.

Impact: several merchant transactions are timing out and failing; conversely our fallback retries are doubling token costs. We're on a hard window: holiday settlement batch starts in ~6 hours for a subset of merchants. We need an ETA and immediate mitigation — is this a reserved throughput shortfall or something else?

Attached is a brief error_snippet with a representative trace (parkline_error_snippet.txt).

Can you confirm:
- whether reserved pool is saturated or throttling at our reservation tier
- whether Redwood can burst additional capacity today and ETA to restore nominal latency
- any recommended short-term routing knobs we should flip on our side to reduce user-visible errors

Please escalate as needed — we may need executive visibility if this can't be resolved quickly.

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability
Parkline Financial

Attachment: parkline_error_snippet.txt (text)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@parklinefin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parkline production timeout wave — seeing 5xx + large p99 latency

Samantha — thanks for the signal and the log excerpt. We see the same metrics on our side; confirmed queue depth growth in Parkline's reserved pool and a spike in evictions at the scheduler boundary.

Immediate actions (in flight):
- I've opened a priority ops bridge and looped infra — David K. is on it to determine whether this is saturation of the reserved allocation vs a serving regression.
- We are standing up an emergency burst (best-effort) while we investigate whether your reserved capacity is being consumed by background workloads.
- Short-term recommendation: flip your routing to the lower-latency hosted fallback for non-sensitive traffic (if you can) and reduce max_retries from 3->1 for the next 2 hours to avoid cascading retries.

I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes. If we need exec escalation I'll notify immediately.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Parkline production timeout wave — need exec decision on burst + credits

Folks — forwarding Parkline's alert. TL;DR: reserved pool for PL-2389 is queuing and we're seeing 5xx/timeouts. Customer needs immediate burst or routing fallback; holiday settlement batch in ~6 hours increases severity.

What I need from leadership now:
- authorization to apply emergency reserved burst (they're on a medium reserved tier) up to +40% for the next 12 hours OR switch specific traffic classes to hosted fallback (we can do per-route).
- guidance on SLA/credit posture if we cannot fully restore within their critical window. Parkline has flagged executive attention if this isn't resolved in the next 2–3 hours.

Current data attached: snapshot of pool metrics timeline from 08/09 (pool-metrics-0908.png) and the customer's error snippet. David is triaging root cause (scheduler heatmap looks noisy).

I'll be on the ops bridge and will update as we learn.

— Tessa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Parkline production timeout wave — need exec decision on burst + credits

Thanks for the heads-up, Tessa & David. We've reviewed the initial telemetry and the ops bridge notes. Actioning the following immediately: 

1) Approve emergency reserved burst for Parkline (PL-2389) up to +45% capacity for the next 10 hours. Infra, please prioritize allocation on nvgpu-optimized racks and favor low-latency kernels. This is billable but we'll discuss crediting if we miss their SLA window.

2) David — please confirm in 10 minutes whether the issue is scheduler-induced queueing (bad fairness across tenants) vs a bad model instantiation on their pool. If it's scheduler fairness, we need a quick patch to isolate Parkline's reservations and avoid requeueing traffic.

3) Marissa / Hannah — prepare a short customer-facing note acknowledging the incident, expected ETA for improvement, and our temporary mitigation (burst + routing guidance). We should also prepare an internal one-page for the CEO (impact, timeline, ask) in case Parkline requests an escalation call.

4) Finance/Commercial: hold off on committing credits; we'll make a call once we have a restore ETA and the postmortem.

I want a status update in 30 minutes and a concrete ETA for full restoration within 2 hours. If not, escalate to cross-functional standup.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Parkline production timeout wave — seeing 5xx + large p99 latency

Tessa / team,

Thanks for moving quickly — we saw a material reduction in 502/503s after you applied the emergency burst and after we temporarily routed non-sensitive flows to hosted fallback. Latency p99 is back down to ~300–350ms for most flows; critical settlement flows are reporting healthy completion.

Two asks while we stabilize:
1) Please share a short postmortem and an ETA for a permanent fix (we'd like to avoid repeat surges during peak batches).
2) Confirm Redwood's position on SLA credits for the impacted window (we circulated our internal impact matrix to product; this will feed into renewal discussions).

I've attached our proposed mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_PL-2389.docx) with suggested checkpoints for capacity gating and rollback criteria. Let's schedule a 30-min postmortem tomorrow.

Appreciate the rapid response.

— Samantha Ortiz
Head of Platform Reliability, Parkline Financial
